title: Colocating ML Inference and Training with Fast GPU Memory Handover
problem: GPU memory becomes a bottleneck when running inference and training workloads simultaneously; inefficient memory transfers between these workloads cause performance degradation and resource underutilization.
motivation: Colocating inference and training on shared GPU resources improves hardware utilization, reduces latency, and decreases total cost of ownership for ML systems.
method: Implements fast GPU memory handover mechanisms that enable efficient memory sharing and data transfer between inference and training kernels. Uses optimized memory management and scheduling to minimize handover overhead and reduce memory fragmentation. Coordinates memory access patterns to avoid contention and enable seamless switching between workloads.
key_novelty: Fast GPU memory handover mechanism enabling efficient, low-latency memory reuse between concurrent inference and training tasks.
contributions: Fast GPU memory handover protocol for seamless inter-workload memory sharing
System design for colocating inference and training on single GPU
Memory management strategies reducing handover overhead
Performance evaluation demonstrating improved GPU utilization and reduced latency
primary_theme: GPU memory optimization for inference-training coexecution
